source.title: Subcritical Signal Propagation at Initialization in Normalization-Free Transformers

record.tranche_reason: The study measures initialization-dependent gradient amplification and early training stability in Derf and pre-LN ViTs, using different models and measures from the original initialization studies.
record.gate_note: Training-stability experiments bear on initialization sensitivity and trainable depth. APJN results measure gradient amplification at initialization, not training classification error. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization sensitivity and early convergence in residual vision transformers. V4 specifies plain networks; these transformers retain residual shortcuts. The study therefore examines a related setting without testing V4 as written. It also tests none of V1–V3 or V5–V6: LayerNorm comparisons are not batch-normalization comparisons, and learning-rate sweeps do not establish stability thresholds or catapult recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive subcritical initialization-time signal propagation for tanh-like residual transformers and find qualitative early-training trends in Derf ViTs consistent with greater sensitivity to depth, weight scale, initial alpha, learning rate, and warmup. Smaller alpha improves stability but can slow convergence. They explicitly do not claim to explain full training dynamics or final performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures APJNs and early training stability in ViTs with Derf versus pre-LN; it does not reproduce the plain-network initialization experiments named in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Derf trainability varies with depth, weight-initialization scale, α initialization, learning rate, and warmup. Smaller learning rates and larger batch sizes shift the reported instability boundary; longer warmup improves performance near it. The experiments are single-run per configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Derf residual ViTs become more sensitive to depth and weight-initialization scale at larger initial alpha, while pre-LN remains comparatively stable. The rows contain early test accuracy; corresponding training-loss curves are explicitly declared left out.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In residual ViTs on CIFAR-100, initial Derf scale and weight variance affect early convergence and the depth at which training becomes pathologically slow.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower learning rates and longer warmup improve early convergence at larger Derf alpha. These experiments do not locate a theoretical stability threshold or demonstrate catapult recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The early optimization stability of Derf residual ViTs depends jointly on initial alpha, learning rate, and warmup.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization-time APJNs grow stretched-exponentially in tanh-like residual transformers and as a power law in pre-LN. Appendix H.1 also states that matching gradient amplification does not ensure matching convergence rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Signal propagation in residual transformers depends on normalization and initialization, but gradient amplification alone does not determine convergence speed.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5(c) and Figure 25 show that overly small initial Derf alpha can slow convergence across several training settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing initial Derf alpha creates a trade-off between early stability and convergence speed in residual ViTs.

record.problems: The authors state that training-stability sweeps are single-run experiments and are qualitative rather than statistically precise. Runs are truncated after 10–20 epochs in the main experiments, and the study uses ViTs on CIFAR-100. Tabulated outcomes are test accuracy rather than training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss curves in Figs. 18–19 and 24–25 are figure-only and not transcribed; supplementary sweeps in Figs. 20–23 and 25 are also figure/table material beyond the selected rows. APJN measurements were left out because they measure initialization-time gradient amplification rather than a version's training outcome.

untested.parts: All: near-zero training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and model-size or regularization conditions.
All: spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
All: plain convolutional networks versus identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup residual networks.
All as written: activation-matched initialization and trainable depth in plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
All: recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, edge-of-stability sharpness dynamics, and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
All: batch normalization versus no batch normalization, higher learning-rate tolerance from batch normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The blanket V4 limits_scope verdict should be removed: a different architecture outside the stated claim is not a demonstrated limitation of that claim. All sweeps are single runs, and low absolute test accuracy is not itself evidence of a partial optimization effect. Fig. 4(b) includes an unrecorded factor-1 baseline: Derf accuracies 24.93%, 24.97%, 22.86%, and 20.11% for alpha 0.4–0.7, versus pre-LN 22.62%. This is useful for the related transformer finding but does not warrant a claim-version missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima across teacher/student widths.
Plain versus identity-shortcut networks; depth-related training error; special initialization of plain tanh networks; Fixup training without normalization.

Plain feedforward networks and orthogonal or activation-matched initialization, including 10,000-layer convolutional networks. The study tests Derf scale and weight-standard-deviation choices in ViTs.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, loss rises and recovery, sharpness behavior, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup residual networks without normalization.

reader_labels.condition: Derf ViT training-stability sweeps on CIFAR-100
reader_labels.reason: Larger depth, weight scale, and α are associated with weaker early training outcomes, while smaller α can also slow convergence; the sweeps are single-run and use test accuracy as the tabulated measure (R1–R38).
